target_customer: Mechanical engineers and hardware teams that produce manufacturing drawings from 3D CAD
problem: Turning 3D designs into annotated 2D manufacturing drawings with GD&T consumes more than 25 percent of a mechanical engineer's time.
business_model: B2B software sold on demo basis, pricing not public
product_category: AI engineering drawing and GD&T automation

founders.name: Alex Rivero
founders.background_notes: Former mechanical engineer; launch post cites Cybertruck, Robotaxi and iPhone 17 work. Education not listed.

founders.name: Louis Liu
education: Studied mechanical engineering, school not named
founders.background_notes: Published machine learning researcher per YC page. One aggregator also credits him with founding Kun; not verified.

competitors.name: DraftAid
competitors.what: Automatic 2D drawing generation from Inventor and SolidWorks models
competitors.funding_then: not found; one low quality aggregator says YC W24

competitors.name: Hanomi
competitors.what: AI platform producing 2D drawings with GD&T from 3D CAD

technical_complexity.rationale: Needs reliable GD&T inference to ASME Y14.5 across CAD formats; company claims 85 percent first pass accuracy, self-reported.

defensibility.rationale: Moat claimed is proprietary pairs of CAD and annotated drawings, but several rivals already target the same wedge and CAD vendors could add it.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent response recorded as of November 2026.

market_need_then: Drawing creation is a recognized time sink for mechanical engineers; company cites over 25 percent of working time. No independent demand data found.

branding.domain_note: Uses rev1.so, not a .com; the name collides with the unrelated Rev1 Ventures accelerator

identity.logo: minimalist wordmark, white on orange on YC page

branding.brand_signature: Claude Code for Mechanical Engineers positioning

brand_strength.rationale: Clear positioning line, but no press about the brand and a name shared with other entities.

outcome_analysis: REV1 is a Winter 2026 YC company that is still active with a two person team. The founders come from Apple and Tesla hardware work, which fits the problem, but competitors target the same drawing automation wedge and no outcome is public yet.
notes: VCBacked and CB Insights both list about 500K (pre-seed or convertible note, around March 2026) with YC as investor; I only saw these in search snippets, so it is unverified and not recorded as a round. Outcome and branding searches returned nothing about a shutdown or the brand.
